document_title: Batch Zero, and the calendar with a hole in it

S1.dek: ERCOT set itself a date to tell service providers how every large load was classified. That date passed 12 days ago.

S2.quote: "ERCOT will not notify each Interconnecting Distribution Service Provider and Transmission Service Provider of how any Large Load is classified in the Batch Zero Interconnection Study by August 7, 2026"
S2.dek: ERCOT gave the market 4 days of notice. The letter has now stood 16 days.

S3.kick: "Update Regarding Batch Zero Timelines and Processes"
S3.qn: No service provider was told how any large load was classified.

S4.o1: of requests to connect to the Texas grid
S4.o2: of the new power requests are data centers
S4.o3: Texas' record peak electricity demand for ERCOT

S5.hook: One office. The same day. Two wordings.
S5.q1: "The PUCT and ERCOT must complete this audit before any data center project moves forward."
S5.q2: "before any additional data centers are approved to move forward"
S5.foot: Marked in red, where the letter narrows what the release says. The signed letter halts approvals. The release halts all forward movement. Both are on the record and they are not interchangeable.

S6.lead: The sector said it will comply.
S6.quote: "I established clear guardrails to ensure data centers protect our electric grid, conserve our water, respect our neighborhoods, and pay their own way ..."
S6.src: Office of the Governor, August 18th · c18
S6.attrib: The Governor's office said so on August 18th. The Data Center Coalition has not published a statement of its own.

S7.quote: "One data center that could not comply chose to end operations before even beginning construction."
S7.src: Office of the Governor, August 18th · c17

S8.hd: What is still open to you.
S8.w1: Open meeting. ERCOT said it would file for a good cause exception ahead of it.
S8.w2: A second open meeting, on the commission's own calendar.
S8.w3: Public comment deadline. The calendar names no docket against it.
S8.w4: The proposed rule on Large Load Demand Management Service. It took a comment on August 18th.
